newsitem.title: INDIA: India's top court rejects politician's bail plea.
newsitem.headline: India's top court rejects politician's bail plea.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed an appeal by a leading politician who sought legal protection against his arrest by federal police in a corruption case.

The nation's highest court rejected an appeal by former Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav against a state court's order refusing to grant him "anticipatory bail", allowed under Indian law to people expecting possible arrest.

"We are in complete agreement with the High Court on the question of anticipatory bail," a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court ruled. "We reject the petition by the appellant against the High Court judgment."

Yadav was forced to resign last Friday after a special court in the Bihar state capital of Patna issued arrest warrants against him and three other politicians in the $280-million scandal involving alleged embezzlement of animal welfare funds.

Yadav, who was indicted by the federal Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in April for his links to the so-called "fodder" scandal, resigned last Friday but immediately named his wife Rabri Devi, a housewife, as his successor.
The CBI says Yadav must be arrested to prevent the tampering of evidence in the case in which the politician says he is innocent.

Devi easily won a confidence vote in the Bihar state assembly on Monday, but her ascent to the office angered opposition parties and posed a challenge to the credibility of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition.

The 15-party United Front alliance decided late on Friday not to admit Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group in its fold, but Gujral has faced criticism for not acting to remove Yadav from office earlier.
